events.title: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season
events.description: Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). As a result of the strong El Niño , it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered. events.title: DNA and vehicle-tracking help French investigators recover stolen Renoirs
events.description: DNA left on a protective painting cover helped investigators recover two stolen Renoirs and uncover what they suspected were preparations for another art heist, a French prosecutor said Monday.

events.title: Many Iranians who go to Turkey to find jobs are exploited
events.description: Desperate Iranians are finding work in Turkey to make ends meet, but many are being exploited and left with nothing but more debt.

events.title: Both Russia and Ukraine are using AI-powered drones on the battlefield
events.description: A Ukrainian company that got rich making smartphone-controlled cameras to watch pets at home now outfits first-person-view drones with an image recognition system powered by artificial intelligence.

events.title: DOJ launches antitrust probe of TV networks. And, Trump says Ukraine needs new leader
events.description: The Justice Department is investigating several TV networks for possible antitrust violations. And, President Trump pressures Ukrainians to elect a new leader.

events.title: Hungary's parliament votes to reverse anti-LGBTQ legislation from Orban era
events.description: Hungary's parliament passed a bill amending the 2021 "child protection law." The move is considered the first significant reversal of Orban's curbs targeting the LGBTQ+ community.

events.title: Spain's King Felipe and Queen Letizia visit Ceuta
events.description: The royal couple have arrived for their first-ever visit to the exclave to show solidarity with residents.

events.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
events.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

events.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
events.description: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

events.title: 'Breaking Bad' actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte dies
events.description: RJ Mitte said his lived experience with cerebral palsy was an asset for his role as Walter White's son Flynn on "Breaking Bad."

events.title: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
events.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.
events.ticker_label: 💥 UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident

events.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
events.description: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

events.title: US economists win Nobel for research helping policymakers navigate crises
events.description: Two American economists, Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, have won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their work on economic stabilisation. Their research helps policymakers and central banks better understand economic fluctuations, manage recessions and inflation, and account for public expectations when shaping economic policy. The prize money, worth around $1.2 million, will be shared equally between the two laureates.

events.title: Pope Leo cancels all public events ahead of lung surgery
events.description: Pope Leo has cancelled all planned public events until Tuesday 20 October, ahead of surgery to remove a small growth on one of his lungs.

events.title: Alleged Irish crime boss will 'vehemently defend' himself in court and apply for bail
events.description: Alleged Irish crime boss Daniel Kinahan will "vehemently defend" the case against him and plans to seek bail, his solicitor says.
